outcome: Give head of e-commerce / merchandising director a governed method to improve orders fulfilled within promised date using POS sales, warehouse stock and store transfers, with final decisions…
overview: Omnichannel Inventory Availability Promise addresses telemetry is noisy or missing, so operators spend time interpreting unrelated warnings in retail and e-commerce operations. The first proof of value uses POS sales, warehouse stock and store transfers. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is orders fulfilled within promised date, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: POS sales, warehouse stock and store transfers; define orders fulfilled within promised date and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Head of E-commerce / Merchandising Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including inject sensor failures, stale data and dependency loss into the pilot.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for orders fulfilled within promised date
